translator: Claude (AI), draft, not reviewed by a Hittitologist
intro: A fragmentary tablet (KUB 41.16 + IBoT 4.309) of an anonymous ritual against plague. The broken text mentions a bull, wicker tables, the deity Lapana, daughter of Appaluwa, an evening rite with fire and offerings described as raw and cooked, and gestures of bowing and placing something in the mouth. The colophon names it a long tablet for when plague arises in a city or in a land.

paras.en: […] this: one bull […] small […] four wicker tables […] … to the lord of the ci[ty](?) […] … I hand over(?).
Then to these gods […] the goddess(?) Lapana, daughter of the god Appaluwa […] … to them(?) they … (ER-anzi, unclear).

[…] they perform […]. When [it becomes] evening […] … they hold the mountains(?) […] they go and kindle a fire […] they … and [they …] it to the gods […] they offer, and on the ground […] raw (and) [co]oked(?) […] they […] […] they let […] … eat(?) […] they burn.
[…] … […] … […] … [… a gap of uncertain length …] […] … […] they place on top […] just so they sp[eak(?) …]
[…] they place on top […] … iškaranda-(?) […] but to the gods [they] bow down […] … and a little […] they place in the mouth; these […] they do likewise … […] three times they do likewise.
[Colophon:] One long tablet, com[plete]. If in a city or in a land plague arises.
